movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Thundurus-T's extremely high Special Attack is elevated to terrifying levels using Nasty Plot, such as OHKOing offensive Heatran after Stealth Rock. Agility complements this by letting Thundurus-T outspeed the entire unboosted metagame. Tera Blast Flying allows Thundurus-T to break past Grass-types like Hydrapple and Zarude, whereas Focus Blast can be used to hit and remove Excadrill, as well as OHKO specially defensive Heatran and Tyranitar after a Nasty Plot. 100 Speed EVs allow Thundurus-T to avoid being revenge killed by threats like Choice Scarf Latios and Ogerpon-C after an Agility. The HP and Special Defense EVs let it survive Soul Dew Latios's Draco Meteor from full HP, with the remaining the EVs invested into Special Attack. Together with Sitrus Berry’s crucial recovery, the bulk investments also enhance Thundurus-T's survivability, ensuring it can safely reach the ideal sweeping position and begin breaking through the opponent’s team. Tera Steel is an alternative to Tera Flying that prevents threats such as Ogerpon-C and Latios from interrupting Thundurus-T's sweep.

Nasty Plot Thundurus-T is a staple of hyper offense teams, which specialize in pressuring the opponent's resources into opening an opportunity for Thundurus-T and other threats to wreak havoc on foes. Thundurus-T is greatly complemented by entry hazard setters, such as Excadrill, which help weaken foes that would tank a +2 Thunderbolt such as bulky Heatran and Fezandipiti. Excadrill and Donphan provide Rapid Spin support, which prevents Thundurus-T from taking Stealth Rock damage. Taunt users such as Heatran and Grimmsnarl pair well with Thundurus-T, as they can also prevent Stealth Rock. Additionally, Grimmsnarl can set up dual screens to provide easier boosting opportunities. Thundurus-T has excellent synergy with fast offensive threats such as Greninja, which can help overwhelm common checks like Latios, Clodsire, and Tinkaton while appreciating Thundurus-T’s ability to pressure bulky Water-type Pokemon like Toxapex. Physical attackers such as Azumarill, Ogerpon, and Ogerpon-C help overpower Ground-types such as Excadrill and Sandy Shocks as well as Unaware users such as Clodsire. Alternatively, setup sweepers like Take Heart Manaphy and Air Balloon Revavroom can capitalize on Clodsire.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Choice Specs Thundurus-T carves out a small niche as a powerful wallbreaker with the tools to wear down and break through many of its supposed checks and counters. With a second STAB option in Volt Switch, Thundurus-T is able to to wear down and keep up momentum against its few defensive checks like Galarian Slowking and Blissey while still securing crucial OHKOs against targets like Moltres, Corviknight, and Alomomola lacking Assault Vest that it intends to threaten out. Tera Blast Fairy grants it the ability to cleanly OHKO Dragon-types like Raging Bolt, Kyurem, and Dragapult while super effectively threatening notable Ground-types like Great Tusk and Ting-Lu. Alternatively, Tera Blast Flying lets Thundurus-T utilize its other STAB typing, giving it the chance to OHKO Rillaboom and Hydrapple, 2HKO Galarian Slowking, and secure an OHKO against IronPress Zamazenta that Tera Fairy barely misses out on guaranteeing. Meanwhile, Tera Blast Ice grants Thundurus-T the coveted BoltBeam coverage combination to devastate Ground-types like Gliscor and even Clodsire while letting it OHKO Dragonite, Raging Bolt, and Dragapult. Grass Knot gives it a way to deal with most Ground-types without needing to Terastallize, taking down Great Tusk and Ursaluna with ease and crucially 2HKOing Ting-Lu after Stealth Rock. Knock Off removes key items like Heavy-Duty Boots from walls like Galarian Slowking, Blissey, and Clodsire; it is also able to remove Assault Vest from the former. Item removal allows Thundurus-T to wear these walls down through repeated switch-ins over the course of a game more easily, particularly when using Volt Switch against the non-Electric-immune checks. However, Knock Off comes at the expense of making Thundurus-T even more reliant on Terastallization for coverage. Focus Blast still deals massive damage to Ting-Lu and OHKOes Kyurem while giving Thundurus-T a way to OHKO even specially defensive Iron Treads, Tyranitar, and Excadrill. If used on rain teams, Thundurus-T is able to slot in a perfectly accurate Thunder over Thunderbolt and use Weather Ball in its last moveslot as coverage for the aforementioned Ground-types. A Timid nature is selected to outrun foes such as Kyurem and Landorus-T. A Modest nature can instead be used to amplify Thundurus-T's breaking power even further to the point that it has a chance to 2HKO Galarian Slowking with Thunderbolt. Thundurus-T's Tera types are primarily chosen for its offensive coverage; however, Tera Fairy crucially lets it completely shut down most Raging Bolt sets in combination with Volt Absorb and resist Kingambit's Sucker Punch. Conversely, Tera Flying and Tera Ice are used for the coverage alone and only serve to worsen Thundurus-T's defensive profile.

Thundurus-T is best used on pivot-heavy teams, slotting onto bulky offense as a dedicated wallbreaker while also finding a home on balance teams that need to make progress against more defensive teams. Thundurus-T's weakness to Stealth Rock and proclivity to pivot around necessitates reliable entry hazard control, making Cinderace and Great Tusk excellent partners with their ability to threaten checks to Thundurus-T like Galarian Slowking, Iron Treads, and, in the case of the latter, Clodsire. Cinderace provides further synergy as another offensive pivot with a propensity to invite in and pivot out of common Electric-weak Pokemon like Alomomola and Moltres, while Great Tusk can give Thundurus-T entry points against defensive Flying-types like Zapdos, Corviknight, and Skarmory. Other forms of hazard control like Galarian Weezing, Iron Treads, and even Hatterene can aid in consistently keeping Stealth Rock off the field while providing defensive utility against Iron Valiant, Galarian Slowking, and Gliscor, respectively. In a similar manner to Cinderace, offensive U-turn users like Scizor and Lokix can be useful in powering a VoltTurn core that brings Thundurus-T in against their own checks like Zapdos and Corviknight. Scizor is notably able to revenge kill Iron Valiant and Enamorus, both of which outspeed and can threaten a weakened Thundurus-T. Alomomola can be used as a more defensive pivot to take a hit and bring Thundurus-T in safely using Flip Turn, a quality replicated by Galarian Slowking with its Chilly Reception; these bulkier pivots help to patch up Thundurus-T's matchups against foes like Cinderace, Iron Valiant, and offensive Zamazenta that can force it out. Thundurus-T's middling Speed tier also gives Ogerpon-W the ability to outspeed and OHKO it after Stealth Rock; other pivoting partners like Rillaboom and Ogerpon can be considered to ease this matchup. These Pokemon additionally check Ground-types like Great Tusk and Ting-Lu looking to punish a Choice-locked Thundurus-T. Ogerpon-W itself can fill this role even better by threatening even more Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus-T, with Ogerpon-W and Thundurus-T forming a wallbreaking and potentially VoltTurn core that can weaken shared checks like Assault Vest Kyurem and Hydrapple. Entry hazards also provide excellent support for Thundurus-T as a breaker, and offensive hazard setters like Landorus-T or Hisuian Samurott can accentuate this further by themselves carrying pivoting moves to bring Thundurus-T in safely. Late-game cleaners like Kingambit and Zamazenta are wincons able to take advantage of the walls Thundurus-T punches through, notably threatening or even setting up against special walls like Galarian Slowking and Blissey, respectively. One partner that can greatly enhance Thundurus-T's power is Drizzle Pelipper; these rain teams enable it to use Weather Ball and a perfectly-accurate Thunder. In return, an immunity to Electric-type moves helps rain partners like Barraskewda and Pelipper itself against Zapdos and Raging Bolt.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Flying

Nasty Plot can be used over Volt Switch to increase Thundurus-T's wallbreaking power, allowing it to easily break Water- and Flying-type teams. Psychic, Sludge Wave, and Thunder Wave are all options that can be used over Focus Blast to achieve different results. Psychic allows Thundurus-T to hit Clodsire and Amoonguss, Sludge Wave can check Hydrapple and Clefable, and Thunder Wave provides Flying teams with a form of speed control by slowing down foes like Dragonite and Gouging Fire. U-turn can be used over Volt Switch to allow Thundurus-T to reliably pivot against foes with an Electric immunity.

movesets.name: Offensive Pivot (Flying)
movesets.description:
Thundurus-T finds a solid niche on Flying teams thanks to its incredible Special Attack, solid Speed, and Electric immunity that allows it to find safe entry against Electric-type moves. Thunderbolt is able to threaten Water- and Flying-types such as Toxapex, Pelipper, and Assault Vest Tornadus-T. Volt Switch helps it pivot out on threats attempting to handle it, such as Hisuian Goodra and Blissey. Grass Knot allows Thundurus-T to hit Ground-types like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Ursaluna that would otherwise wall it. Finally, Focus Blast remove Steel- and Rock-types like Iron Treads, Archaludon, and Tyranitar.

Skarmory and Gliscor provide excellent support to Thundurus-T, being able to deal with Rock-types such as Iron Boulder, Kleavor, and Terrakion reliably, as well as setting entry hazards to chip down threats like Hisuian Goodra and Archaludon. Skarmory can also support Thundurus-T by dealing with Ice-types like Weavile and Mamoswine with Body Press. Corviknight can similarly check Ice- and Rock-types with Iron Head and Body Press, use Defog to remove Stealth Rock if Thundurus-T loses its Heavy-Duty Boots, and give Thundurus-T safe entry with U-turn. Articuno provides a comfortable answer to Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus, which can handle Thundurus-T's Grass Knot. Furthermore, Articuno can come in on special threats such as Kyurem and Greninja that Thundurus-T cannot handle. Dragonite acts a physical wallbreaker, handling specially defensive walls like Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Clodsire, while appreciating Thundurus-T's ability to eliminate physically defensive walls such as Galarian Weezing and Sableye. Choice Scarf Enamorus can threaten Dragon-type foes attemping to handle Thundurus-T, such as Dragapult, Kyurem, and Choice Band Roaring Moon. Landorus forms a special wallbreaking core, removing Fire-types like Skeledirge, Hisuian Arcanine, and Heatran with ease. Landorus can also run a Choice Scarf and use U-turn to create a VoltTurn core with Thundurus-T while also OHKOing the Ogerpon formes with Sludge Wave after Stealth Rock damage.

movesets.name: Pivot
movesets.description:
• Thanks to Volt Absorb, Thundurus-T is an excellent offensive pivot that makes masterful use of Terastallization!

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot is highly recommended for dealing massive damage to Ground-types, such as Ting-Lu and Ursaluna, without Terastallizing in addition to being a secondary attack to hit Urshifu-R while Choice locked into an attack.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast has reliability issues, but it's Thundurus-T's best shot of dealing big damage to Hisuian Goodra and Wo-Chien.

  • Sludge Bomb: Sludge Bomb is a more niche option, giving Thundurus-T a more reliable way to deal damage to Wo-Chien and Meowscarada at the cost of doing nothing to Hisuian Goodra.

  • Timid versus Modest: Timid is the best nature, allowing Thundurus-T to outspeed key threats, such as Urshifu-R, and at least Speed tie with opposing Thundurus-T. Modest is usable with Choice Specs, allowing Thundurus-T to outspeed up to Jolly Baxcalibur and Great Tusk, and the extra power can be handy in some situations, such as usually 2HKOing specially defensive Clodsire with Tera Blast Flying.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Thundurus-T is perfectly fine with its base typing, it makes such good use of Terastallization that it'll often Terastallize.

  • Flying: Tera Flying makes Tera Blast a powerful STAB option with very few resistances while gaining no extra weaknesses thanks to Volt Absorb.

  • Ice: Not only does Tera Ice give Thundurus-T powerful coverage against Ground- and Grass-types like Landorus-T and Wo-Chien, it also gives an important resistance to Iron Bundle's and Chien-Pao's Ice-type attacks.

  • Water: Tera Water is a fantastic defensive option, turning Thundurus-T into an excellent check against Regieleki and Zapdos while still giving it a good coverage option against Landorus-T. However, it still retains Thundurus-T's weakness to Freeze-Dry.

Items

  • Choice Specs versus Choice Scarf: Choice Specs makes Thundurus-T difficult to wall without an extremely sturdy special wall, with even Pokemon like Clodsire and Cresselia at risk of a 2HKO. Choice Scarf, on the other hand, allows Thundurus-T to double as a good revenge killer, outspeeding major threats like Iron Bundle and Chien-Pao.

  • Assault Vest: While Thundurus-T isn't known for its bulk, Volt Absorb means Assault Vest makes Thundurus-T more effective at checking other Electric-types, especially when using bulkier EV spreads.

Bulkier EV Spreads

  • 20 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 228 Spe with Timid: This Assault Vest spread outspeeds both Urshifu formes and takes 70% maximum from Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry without sacrificing power.

  • 188 SpA / 68 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid or Modest**: This spread is optimized for Assault Vest, letting Thundurus-T survive Timid Choice Specs Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry without Terastallizing.

Minor Optimizations
  • 0-3 Attack IV: Foes that commonly run Foul Play such as Amoonguss and Rotom-W have more powerful moves to use against Thundurus-T, but there's no drawback to minimizing Foul Play's damage.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
• Thundurus-T's massive Special Attack stat and array of immunities make it a good user of Nasty Plot.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot is integral for potentially OHKOing physically defensive Ting-Lu after a boost and usually OHKOing offensive Ursaluna.

  • Life Orb versus Sitrus Berry: Life Orb is great for wallbreaking, allowing Thundurus-T to potentially OHKO Ting-Lu with a boosted Grass Knot. Sitrus Berry is still a good option, though allowing Thundurus-T to instantly restore some health after being hit by Ruination, as long as its maximum HP is an even number.

Other Options

  • Substitute: When paired with Tera Water, Substitute lets Thundurus-T set up on Garganacl.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast's unreliability makes it hard to recommend for most teams, but it's the only way Thundurus-T will break through Hisuian Goodra without Terastallization.

  • Taunt: Giving up coverage is risky, but Taunt shuts down a lot of defensive counterplay against Thundurus-T such as Whirlwind Ting-Lu and Toxic Clodsire.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Thundurus-T's typing is totally functional for sweeping and wallbreaking, but Terastallization makes it far harder to revenge kill thanks to Volt Absorb.

  • Flying: Tera Flying gives Thundurus-T a powerful STAB option, letting it cleave through specially bulky foes, like Water Absorb Clodsire, particularly easily.

  • Water: While Tera Water does leave Thundurus-T vulnerable to certain Pokemon, such as Water Absorb Clodsire and Hisuian Goodra, it's a fantastic defensive Tera type that lets it deal with other common Electric-types that Terastallize like Regieleki and Zapdos.

  • Ice: Tera Ice is a great offensive option, letting Thundurus-T cleave through most Ground-types that aren't weak to Grass such as Landorus-T and Clodsire. Thundurus-T even makes good defensive use of it, resisting Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry.

Bulkier EV Spreads
  • 108 HP / 4 Def / 140 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid: This EV spread lets Thundurus-T survive Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry, if it doesn't have an offensive item, making it a good choice for more defensive items Thundurus-T may use such as Sitrus Berry.
Minor Optimizations
  • 0-3 Attack IV: Thundurus-T isn't getting hit by Foul Play that often, but a lower Attack IV is marginally useful regardless.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description: Bolstering an incredible Special Attack stat combined with a great movepool makes Thundurus-T an extremely threatening wallbreaker. Focus Blast nails foes such as Hisuian Goodra, Volt Absorb Empoleon, and Volt Absorb Corviknight. Psychic hits Great Tusk and Iron Hands, while Grass Knot can let Thundurus-T lure in and take out Swampert while still hitting Great Tusk for super effective damage. Nasty Plot boosts Thundurus-T's Special Attack to nuclear levels, allowing it to OHKO Hisuian Goodra and Blissey with Focus Blast after slight chip damage. Fast specially offensive pivots such as Iron Moth, Choice Scarf Azelf, and Latios appreciate Thundurus-T's incredible wallbreaking power, as they can take advantage of weakened special walls such as Swampert, Manaphy, and Meloetta. Thundurus-T loves slow, defensive pivots such as Corviknight, physically defensive Manaphy, and Swampert, as they can take on faster threats such as Iron Boulder, Chien-Pao, and Azelf, which all threaten to KO it, while also being able to safely pivot it in. Entry hazard Removal from the likes of Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Mandibuzz is also helpful, as Thundurus-T is very vulnerable to Stealth Rock. Sticky Web support from a teammate like Smeargle or Ribombee is another option, as it can give Thundurus-T the opportunity to outpace previously mentioned revenge killers.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 4 onwards

Price Range: 11-12 points

Tera Price Range: 13-14 points

Overview: Thundurus-T boasts both incredible Special Attack and strong setup options, making it a solid wallbreaker that can also be used as a wincon. However, its mediocre bulk, average Speed tier, lack of Flying-type STAB moves, and weakness to Stealth Rock keep it fairly inconsistent. Thankfully, Terastallization solves many of Thundurus-T's issues, heavily boosting its performance in battle. While Thundurus-T is still usable without Tera, it is very elevated by the mechanic and is usually drafted with the intention of it being a Tera Captain.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Offensive Pivot: Thundurus-T's sheer power can force many slower foes to switch out, and it can take advantage of this by gaining momentum with an incredibly strong STAB Volt Switch or U-turn when facing Electric-type immunities.

Wallbreaker: Thundurus-T's immense Special Attack, powerful Electric-type STAB moves, and decent coverage moves let it break through many defensive Pokemon. These sets will run damage-boosting items for optimal damage output and an offensive Tera type for additional coverage or a power boost to its existing coverage.

Setup Sweeper: By using Nasty Plot and Agility—together or separately—Thundurus-T can boost its offenses and sweep games as a strong wincon. These sets will usually opt for a defensive Tera type to better create setup opportunities.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Thunderbolt, Discharge, Volt Switch, Thunder, Wildbolt Storm

Setup Moves: Nasty Plot, Agility

Utility Moves: U-turn, Knock Off, Taunt, Substitute, Brick Break, Thunder Wave

Coverage: Dark Pulse, Flash Cannon, Focus Blast, Grass Knot, Psychic, Sludge Bomb, Sludge Wave, Weather Ball

Niche Moves

Sunny Day / Rain Dance: Manual weather-setting moves can be paired with Weather Ball to give Thundurus-T access to a strong Fire-type or Water-type attack.

Acrobatics: Acrobatics is Thundurus-T's strongest Flying-type STAB move. It compromises Thundurus-T's item slot, but this can sometimes be worth it if Thundurus-T would like a Flying-type attack without committing to Tera Blast Flying. Acrobatics can also be combined with other physically-focused moves like Bulk Up and Supercell Slam.

Foul Play: Foul Play can be used on Choice Scarf sets to revenge kill Attack-boosting setup sweepers that Thundurus-T can't OHKO with its regular attacks.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots negates Thundurus-T's weakness to Stealth Rock, which protects it as it pivots in and out of the field during the battle.

Choice Specs: Choice Specs maximizes Thundurus-T's damage output, making it a potent wallbreaker.

Choice Scarf: Thundurus-T can remedy its mediocre Speed somewhat with a Choice Scarf, allowing it to outpace unboosted offensive threats. Notably, Choice Scarf lets Thundurus-T outspeed many of the common Speed-boosting and Choice Scarf members of the base 100 Speed tier at +1.

Damage-boosting Items: Items like Life Orb or Expert Belt can be used to increase Thundurus-T's damage output without locking it into a move.

Niche Items

Assault Vest: Thundurus-T may be frail, but its defensive typing combined with Volt Absorb is very solid, and it can patch up its special bulk with an Assault Vest to defensively check some special attackers like Zapdos and Tornadus-T.

Resistance Berries: While Thundurus-T does have low bulk, a resistance Berry can still help it survive a super effective attack, allowing it to either set up without fear or revenge kill a foe.

Tera

Thundurus-T benefits a lot from Tera, so it should mostly be drafted as a Tera Captain. While it is usable without Tera, it gains a lot from the mechanic both offensively and defensively. Offensively, Tera Electric powers up its strong Thunderbolt and Volt Switch even further, Tera Flying gives it access to strong special Flying-type STAB move, and it can use Tera types like Ground, Water, and Fairy to gain coverage it normally doesn't have. Alternatively, it can use a defensive Tera type like Poison or Steel to give wincon sets more opportunities to set up.

Draft Strategy

Thundurus-T is most effective as a Tera Captain, so it is typically drafted as one. It is relatively cheap compared to other good Tera Captains, so it can be paired with a second decent Tera Captain. With that being said, Thundurus-T is not strong enough to be the centerpiece of a draft and should only be taken if it fits a team's already established structure.

Tera-banned High-value Pokemon: Thundurus-T really would like to be a Tera Captain, so it's most efficient to pair it with top-tier Pokemon that cannot Tera anyway, such as Iron Valiant, Palafin, and Darkrai.

Entry Hazard Removal: Thundurus-T would prefer not to use Heavy-Duty Boots all the time, so entry hazard removal support from Pokemon like Great Tusk, Donphan, and Excadrill is appreciated, as it alleviates its need for Heavy-Duty Boots.

Speed Control: Thundurus-T leaves much to be desired in terms of Speed, so a high base Speed Pokemon like Meowscarada, Greninja, or Iron Bundle is appreciated to keep the fast offensive Pokemon that outspeed Thundurus-T in check.

Strong Physical Offensive Pivot: Thundurus-T can form a powerful VoltTurn offensive core with a strong physical attacker like Urshifu-R, Cinderace, or Roaring Moon. This can help pressure the opposing team and wear down foes, allowing either Thundurus-T or its teammates to clean late-game.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Thundurus-T lacks Ground-type coverage, and Electric-types resist Thundurus-T's STAB moves. While Thundurus-T is immune to Electric-type attacks thanks to Volt Absorb, it cannot do much to Electric-types in return, so they will most often beat Thundurus-T head-to-head with their coverage moves. Some examples include Raging Bolt, Rotom-H, and Bellibolt, but opposing Tera Captains may use Tera Electric to deal with Thundurus-T as well.

Faster Offensive Threats: Thundurus-T's Speed tier is mediocre, leaving it outsped by a large portion of the metagame. Combined with its low bulk, this makes Thundurus-T struggle when dealing with offensive pressure.

Stealth Rock: Thundurus-T doesn't want to use Heavy-Duty Boots all the time, and Stealth Rock limits its effectiveness as an offensive pivot. It will need to rely on its teammates for entry hazard removal support.

movesets.name: Electrium Z (Flying)
movesets.description: Thundurus-T makes for a great setup sweeper on Flying teams thanks to its access to Agility, high Special Attack, and great coverage. Hidden Power Ice forms a great BoltBeam combination with Thunderbolt, threatening Ground-types such as the Landorus formes, Gliscor, and Garchomp, with the removal of the former two allowing it to sweep Flying teams late-game. Grass Knot handles certain Ground-types better than Hidden Power Ice such as Great Tusk, Gastrodon, and physically defensive Ting-Lu. Agility allows Thundurus-T to outspeed and threaten normally faster foes such as Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and rain-boosted Mega Swampert. Gigavolt Havoc allows Thundurus-T to immediately remove bulky threats such as Rotom-W, Hatterene, and Mega Gallade as well as hindrances to its sweep like specially defensive Celesteela, Toxapex, and Ogerpon-W. Gliscor and Landorus make for great partners, as they alleviate pressure from Thundurus-T, cover the Electric matchup, and set up entry hazards. Additionally, Gliscor provides pivoting via U-turn and removes items such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite and Zapdos, while Landorus's coverage allows it to cover threats such as Mega Charizard X, Tyranitar, and Tapu Bulu. Entry hazard removal from Corviknight and Mantine is appreciated by Thundurus-T due to its vulnerability to Stealth Rock. Additionally, Corviknight and Celesteela handle Fairy- and Rock-types like Tapu Bulu, Mega Diancie, and Iron Boulder. Early-game wallbreakers such as Tornadus-T and Mega Charizard Y remove walls that Thundurus-T struggles with such as Mega Venusaur and Ferrothorn. In return, they appreciate Thundurus-T's Electric immunity. Choice Scarf Enamorus provides great speed control, with it potentially being able to sweep through Dragon and Dark teams that lack a proper answer; it also provides Healing Wish support to potentially re-enable a sweep from Thundurus-T. In return, it handles Steel-types for Thundurus-T like Corviknight and Mega Scizor. Thundurus-T's ability to threaten walls such as Toxapex, Great Tusk, and Ting-Lu can also enable other sweepers like Dragonite, Mega Aerodactyl, and Galarian Moltres to start a sweep of their own.
